_description: Game-design decisions for the RPG layer: character generation, mechanics, type boundaries. Append only; supersede with a new entry instead of editing.

title: Split character generation into mechanical and narrative layers
context: Need character output that fits the campaign setting without coupling mechanics to AI. Alternatives considered: single AI call for everything; fixed random tables for identity.
decision: Mechanical (deterministic randomizer) and narrative (AI identity) are separate layers in the generation pipeline.
rationale: Fixed identity tables produce setting-agnostic results. A cyberpunk game needs cyberpunk names, not fantasy ones. AI generates identity contextually.
consequences_positive: Mechanics are instant and testable; identity always fits the setting

title: Removed random identity tables (CAM-7)
context: Originally identity was sourced from random tables; this decoupled identity from setting. Alternative considered: keep random tables as fallback.
decision: All identity is AI-generated; random identity tables are removed.
rationale: Random tables for names/weapons would ignore campaign setting. AI generation produces contextually appropriate identities for any genre combination.

title: Branded types (GeneratedText, I18nKey) to distinguish content origins
context: AI-generated strings, i18n keys, and raw strings were too easy to confuse. Alternative considered: plain strings with naming conventions.
decision: Use branded TypeScript types in shared/types/utils.ts to mark AI output (GeneratedText) and i18n keys (I18nKey).
rationale: Type system enforces that AI-generated text and i18n keys are never confused. Prevents bugs where a raw string is used where a translation key is expected.
consequences_positive: Compile-time safety for content type boundaries

title: Party size is 1-4 with no duplicate combos
context: 9 total combos (3 archetypes x 3 suits). Alternatives considered: allow duplicates; max 6 players.
decision: Party size is 1-4. No duplicate archetype+suit combos by construction (selector shows all 9; each can only be picked once).
rationale: Max 4 ensures variety. No duplicates by construction since the selector shows all 9 and each can only be picked once.
consequences_positive: Clean party composition with guaranteed uniqueness
